traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 369 Zingiberaceae: perennial herbs, usually aromatic, with creeping tuberous rhizomes; leaves in two ranks, sheathing at the base, the blade large with many close parallel veins running obliquely from the midrib; flowers mostly bisexual, irregular or lopsided; perianth of 6 in two whorls, the outer calyx-like, the inner petal-like; one fertile stamen, often with petal-like staminodes; ovary inferior, of 3 (rarely 2) cells; fruit fleshy and staying shut, or a capsule opening in three.
